questions.q: What is a transducer?
options: A device that converts energy from one form to another
A type of sensor that detects only energy
A part of a computer processor
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): a transducer 'converts the energy from one form to the energy in another form'.

questions.q: What does sensor accuracy refer to?
options: The correctness of the output compared to a standard value
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): accuracy 'is about the correctness of the output compared to a superior system' - only option matching.

questions.q: What is an active sensor?
options: A sensor that can only sense physical changes
A sensor that operates without an external power source
A sensor that independently senses the input
A sensor that operates without any energy consumption
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): 'active sensors are the ones which can independently sense the input'.

questions.q: What does ‘Actuator’ primarily refer to in IIoT systems?
options: A device that converts signals into physical action
A device that enhances signal strength
questions.explanation: Lecture 01 (Sensing & Actuation): actuator takes a control signal plus energy and produces mechanical action.

questions.q: Zigbee technology is popular for ________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): ZigBee offers low power, low data rate, medium range with mesh as the most used topology.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about 6LoWPAN?
options: It is used for high-power industrial networks
It enables IPv6 packets over low-power wireless networks
It’s a standard for satellite communications
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 6LoWPAN 'is about use of IPv6 over ... low power wireless personal area networks'.

questions.q: Near Field Communication (NFC) is typically used for:
options: Short-range wireless interaction between electronic devices
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): NFC works 'within close proximity', range < 10 cm.

questions.q: Which of the following actuators work on the principle of compression and decompression?
questions.explanation: Not in the IIoT transcript; Misra's IoT-course/textbook actuator section describes hydraulic actuators as working on compression and decompression of fluids.

questions.q: ISA 100.11a is significant in IIoT because it _______________.
options: Focuses on wireless network technology for industrial automation
Is used for long-range satellite communications
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): ISA 100.11a 'is a standard that is used for wireless network technology ... primarily focuses on automation in industrial environments'.

questions.q: What is the primary function of IEEE 802.15.4 in IoT?
options: Establishing low-rate wireless personal area networks
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): 802.15.4 provides PHY/MAC framework for low-power, low-rate wireless personal area networks.

questions.q: Z-Wave technology is best suited for __________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 03 (IoT Connectivity Part II): Z-wave 'is useful particularly for home automation application'.

questions.q: What is the maximum data rate possible in Wireless HART?
questions.explanation: Lecture 02 (IoT Connectivity Part I): WirelessHART 'using data rates of up to about 250 kbps'.

questions.q: QoS 2 in MQTT is also known as ____________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): 'QoS 2 ... is about exactly once delivery'.

questions.q: CoAP works on Request/Response framework based on the _______ architecture.
questions.explanation: Lecture 05 (IoT Networking Part II): CoAP works on top of UDP (with DTLS).

questions.q: Infra-red sensor is an example of __________.
questions.explanation: Infra-red sensors detect light (IR radiation) - an optical sensor; not discussed in the lecture.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): Industry 4.0 uses 'artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber physical systems'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a physical megatrend?
questions.explanation: Lecture 06 (The Fourth Revolution): physical megatrends are autonomous vehicles, 3D printing, advanced robotics, new materials - cloud is not.

questions.q: How does Industry 4.0 enhance sustainability in manufacturing industries?
options: By reducing the use of digital technologies
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): Industry 4.0 'incorporates globalization and emerging issues' for sustainability.

questions.q: What is a crucial aspect of Supply Chain Management (SCM) in sustainable manufacturing?
options: Considering environmental concerns such as climate change, contamination, and resource consumption
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): SCM 'has many additional environmental concerns ... climate change, contamination, resource consumption'.

questions.q: What role does ICT play in the manufacturing industry?
options: Serving as the main nervous system of any manufacturing industry
Discouraging the sharing of information between customer, producer, and supplier
Eliminating the need for enterprise resource planning
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): ICT is 'the backbone of most of the modern manufacturing industries' (slide: main nervous system).

questions.q: What characterizes an emerging market in the context of Industry 4.0?
options: Markets that are fully developed and static
Markets that meet the standards of newly developed innovative products
Markets that exclusively focus on traditional products
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): emerging markets: 'markets are able to meet the standards of newly developed innovative products'.

questions.q: What is the primary focus of the Lean Production System?
options: Overworking the employees to boost production
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean 'mainly focuses on addressing the customer's needs directly'.

questions.q: Which among the following are aspects of socio-economic issues of sustainability in Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 07 (Sustainability Assessment of Manufacturing Industry): regulation/sustainability issues are economic, social and environmental.

questions.q: The Lean Production System mainly focuses on the customer’s need. Which company is credited for the development of Lean Production System?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean 'has its origin in the Toyota motor corporation'.

questions.q: What is a major concern in implementing Lean Production in the context of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 08 (Lean Production System): lean in Industry 4.0 concerns 'the integration of humans in the plant'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a benefit of smart and connected products?
options: Rapid increment in the sale price of a product
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): benefits are faster, cheaper, better usage, improved recall, decreased environmental impact, smart supply chain - not price increase.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a fundamental building block of a smart and connected business in the context of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 09 (Smart and Connected Business Perspective): building blocks are 'customer values, blueprint of profits, key resources and key processes' - all options are blocks.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of smart factories?
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): advantages include 'improving the quality ... improving the safety'.

questions.q: How is information technology utilized in smart factories?
options: For smart software applications and to control processes
questions.explanation: Lecture 10 (Smart Factories): IT provides 'smart software, smart hardware, smart management, smart monitoring, smart control'.

questions.q: Communication, trust and capital with respect to the created values play an important role in IIoT business model.
questions.explanation: Not found in Weeks 1-2 transcripts; consistent with the course's IIoT business-model material (value creation relies on communication, trust and capital) - True.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a feature of Cyber-Physical Systems?
questions.explanation: L11: CPS features are reactive computation, concurrency, feedback control, real-time computation; CPS are networked, not standalone.

questions.q: In the context of CPS in Smart Grid, what is the full form of DAU?
questions.explanation: L11 lists smart-grid CPS 'PMUs Phasor Measurement Units, Data Acquisition Unit'; of the given options only Data Aggregation Unit fits DAU.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of CPS’s “5C Architecture” for Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L11: the 5Cs are connection, conversion, cyber, cognition, configuration; compatibility is not one.

questions.q: What are the key parts enabling collaboration productivity in Industry 4.0?
options: IT Proliferation, Single Source of Truth, Industrialization, Coordination
Financial Analysis, Market Research, Legal Compliance, Public Relations
Human Resources, Sales Targets, Customer Feedback, Advertising
Supply Chain Management, Quality Control, Cost Reduction, Branding
questions.explanation: L12: collaboration productivity enabled by key parts 'IT, single source of truth, industrialization, and coordination'.

questions.q: What does ‘PLM’ stand for in the context of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L12: PLM = product lifecycle management.

questions.q: What does the Technique ‘ABC’ in PLM stand for?
questions.explanation: L12 techniques and methods: 'activity based costing, concurrent engineering, design for sustainability, and lifecycle assessment'.

questions.q: In which fields are AR and VR used in Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: L13: AR/VR use cases 'machining and production ... education, training, collaboration, assembly line'.

questions.q: Which among the following is one type of categorization of AR?
questions.explanation: L13: AR types include 'marker less augmented reality'.

questions.q: What type of AR uses visual markers for outcomes?
questions.explanation: L13: 'Marker based augmented reality gives an outcome when the reader is sensed by the camera and the visual marker'.

questions.q: What type of knowledge is used in AI techniques?
questions.explanation: L14: forms of knowledge are procedural/operational, declarative/relational, and heuristic.

questions.q: What is the use of AI in IIoT?
options: Machine safety, efficient product lifecycle, efficient manufacturing processes, and others
questions.explanation: L14: 'machine safety, efficient products lifecycle, efficient manufacturing processes, these could be achieved with the help of AI'.

questions.q: Which of the following characterizes Big Data?
options: Consists of structured and non-structured data
questions.explanation: L15: big data is 'non-structured as well as structured data'.

questions.q: What does a distributed file system in Big Data ensure?
options: Consistency, accessibility, and fault tolerance of data
questions.explanation: Distributed file systems (GFS/HDFS, L15) store large files across nodes for consistent, accessible and fault-tolerant storage; other options are negatives.

questions.q: Suppose you write a program which uses an API to collect data continuously from LinkedIn and Facebook. You then wish to analyze such data. What type of big data source are you using?
questions.explanation: Data pulled from third-party platforms (LinkedIn/Facebook APIs) is an external data source, not internal enterprise data.

questions.q: What does Cybersecurity protect?
questions.explanation: L16: 'how to protect the hardware, how to protect the software and how to protect the data'.

questions.q: What is the focus of Network Security?
options: Protecting network architecture from unauthorized access and improper use
Protecting only the company CEO’s information
Solely focused on securing paper documents
questions.explanation: L16: network security protects the network architecture from unauthorized access and improper use.

questions.q: What does the CIA Triad in Cybersecurity stand for?
questions.explanation: L16: 'C stands for confidentiality, I stands for integrity and A stands for availability'.

questions.q: What are the key differences between IIoT and traditional Automation?
options: Ubiquitous sensing, advanced analytics, IT tools, and methodologies
Limited to the type of machinery used
questions.explanation: L17: differences with respect to ubiquitous sensing, advanced analytics, and IT tools and methodologies.

questions.q: What are the benefits of deploying sensors and actuators in IIoT?
options: To control, enhance, and optimize various functions
questions.explanation: L17: 'in IIoT sensors and actuators have been also used everywhere to control, enhance, and optimize various functions'.

questions.q: How does IIoT benefit the mining industry?
questions.explanation: L17: IIoT in mining benefits 'in terms of having early disaster warning'.

questions.q: What is the Third Wave in GE’s industrial level innovation?
questions.explanation: L18: 'the third wave ... is this industrial internet'.

questions.q: Scarcity of non-renewable sources of energy pose a significant challenge with respect to energy consumption for the future smart industries and industrial internet?
questions.explanation: Not in the W4 transcripts (L7 discusses finite non-renewable energy). Scarcity of non-renewable energy is a recognized challenge for future smart industries, so True.

questions.q: What was the negative effect of the Industrial Revolution?
questions.explanation: L18: industrial revolution 'increased the amount of waste products ... adverse effects on the environment'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not one of the three key elements of the Industrial Internet?
questions.explanation: L18: three key elements are 'intelligent machines ... advanced analytics, and ... people at work'.

questions.q: How is a smart sensor defined according to IEEE 1451 standard?
options: Sensor with standardized physical connection for communication
Sensor without the need for a power supply
questions.explanation: L19: smart sensors have 'small memory and standardized physical connection ... as per the IEEE 1451 standard'.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the MRAA library in Intel IoT devices?
questions.explanation: L19: 'MRAA component which is a low-level skeleton library for communication in the GNU Linux platform'.

questions.q: What is a key aspect of the design philosophy for IIoT in industrial processes?
options: Prioritizing manual control over automated systems
questions.explanation: L20 Industrial Processes Part 1: 'Interoperability is about facilitating communication between heterogeneous objects'.

questions.q: What is a feature of the Autonomous Pull Economy in Industrial Process 4.0?
questions.explanation: L20: autonomous pull economy benefits are 'end-to-end automation facility, updated demand information, low waste generation'.

questions.q: Considering the future architecture of the smart Industrial plant, which among the following layers is responsible for autonomous decision making, machine learning and decision support system?
questions.explanation: L20: in the futuristic plant's 5C layers, 'the cognitive layer ... systems for optimized decision making', which best fits decision support and autonomous decisions.

questions.q: What is a key technology driver in Amazon’s Smart Warehousing?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Amazon smart warehousing tech-drivers are 'warehouse automation and the human-machine interaction'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not covered under the domain of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Industry 4.0 sectors listed: smart robotics, intelligent manufacturing, smart warehousing, smart logistics, etc.; deforestation is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following IIoT platforms is used by Hitachi?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Hitachi 'have the Lumada IoT platform'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a type of business model for IoT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): IoT business models are subscription, outcome-based, asset-sharing and IoT-as-a-service; no loss-sharing model.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of the Subscription Model in IoT?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): subscription model advantage - 'it is a predictable kind of model' generating recurring revenue.

questions.q: Which is a critical challenge of the IoT-as-a-Service model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): IoT-as-a-Service challenges: 'product compatibility, maintaining data accuracy, security of data'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT offered by a Service-Oriented IIoT Business Model?
options: On-demand services backed by cloud-based Business Models
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): service-oriented model offers data utilization/aggregation/analysis, on-demand cloud-based services and self-service interfaces; CapEx investment is not mentioned.

questions.q: Process Oriented Business Model is a __________ business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2) stresses that cloud-based, service-oriented and process-oriented models are interlinked (process-oriented uses data from the others); 'Hybrid' is the only fitting option.

questions.q: What is IIRA?
options: A standard architecture for IIoT Systems
A scheme for corporate tax rebate
A package for installing IIoT Software
An internship program for IoT enthusiasts
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): IIRA is 'sort of a standard architecture that IIoT systems globally tend to use'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about IIRA?
options: Safety is not a concern in the IIRA infrastructure,
The IIRA infrastructure is proposed by the IIC Technology Working Group
The IIRA infrastructure maps application technologies
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'for the IIRA one of the central thematic concerns is the safety' - so the 'safety is not a concern' statement is the incorrect one.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of the three-tier architecture pattern of IIRA?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): three-tier pattern has 'the edge layer, the platform layer and the enterprise layer'; no fog layer.

questions.q: What are the IIRA Viewpoints?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): viewpoints are business, usage, functional and implementation.

questions.q: The elements of an activity in IIRA are ___________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'The elements of an activity are trigger, workflow, effects and constraints'.

questions.q: In the Business Viewpoint of IIRA, what are fundamental capabilities?
options: High-level specifications essential for business tasks
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'Fundamental capabilities are high level specifications, which are essential to complete business tasks'.

questions.q: With respect to the IIRA functional domain, industrial actuation falls under which of the following domains?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): control domain functions include sensing, 'actuation writing data and controlling signals into an actuator' and communication.

questions.q: Which of the following temperature sensors generates an analog voltage proportional to the temperature?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): LM35 is an analog sensor whose output voltage is proportional to Celsius temperature.

questions.q: What are the key components of an IoT Sensing Device?
options: Sensor, Processor, Wireless Communication Module, Power Management Unit
Battery, Processor, Universal Serial Bus, Visual Display Unit
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): IoT sensing device = sensor, processor, power management unit, wireless communication module.

questions.q: What kind of sensor is ADXL335?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): 'ADXL335 accelerometer sensor'.

questions.q: “MOS gas sensor depend on the thermal energy for its operation which is supplied with a heater.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): chemi-resistive gas sensors 'depend on the thermal energy for its operation which is basically supplied through some heater'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a probable application of Gas Sensors?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): applications: air-quality monitoring, toxic gas leakage detection, automotive exhaust, alcohol breath test; not motion tracking.

questions.q: What is meant by the Sensitivity of a Gas Sensor?
options: Change in the output signal for a unit change in gas concentration
Ability to detect a particular gas in a mixture of different gases
Ability to provide consistent output over a long period of time
The time taken by the sensor to stabilize its response
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): sensitivity is 'the change in the output signal, with respect to the unit change in the input' (gas concentration).

questions.q: The ModBus-TCP protocol defines two units in the data frame. One of them is Protocol Data Unit. What is the other one?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'the protocol defines two units in the data frame; one is ... the application data unit, the other ... the protocol data unit'.

questions.q: With respect to sensors, a camera which can simultaneously sense the ambient temperature as well as capture live video recordings is a type of ________ sensor.
questions.explanation: Sensor that senses both scalar (temperature) and multimedia (video) data is a hybrid sensor (scalar/multimedia/hybrid classification from Misra's IoT material).

questions.q: EtherNet/IP defines two primary types of communications. What are those?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'in EtherNet/IP there are two types of communications; explicit and implicit'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about Profinet?
options: Profinet is the standard for industrial Ethernet
Profinet can not be used for process control or process measurement
Profinet uses NRT, RT and IRT communication channels
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): Profinet 'is used for process control, process measurement', so the 'cannot be used' statement is incorrect.

questions.q: Modbus-RTU is a serial protocol that follows the ________ architecture.
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): Modbus RTU 'provides the serial communication between the master/slave'.

questions.q: Which of the following network topologies is used by Profibus?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): 'the bus topology is very popular in Profibus'.

questions.q: In the context of DeviceNet, CAN is the acronym for ___________.
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): DeviceNet 'is based on the standard controller area network protocols'.

questions.q: How shorter TTL is achieved in uRLLC?
options: By reducing Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing symbols in TTL
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): shorter TTI via 'smaller slot lengths ... reducing the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing symbols, reducing symbol duration'.

questions.q: What is the frequency spectrum of mmWave Communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): mmWave communication is in 'the spectrum 30 to 300 Giga hertz band'.

questions.q: Which of the following stands for LP in LPWAN?
questions.explanation: 'low power wide area network ... LPWAN' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: “We need to pay a license fee to use LoRa in the 868 MHz radio frequency band in Europe.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: 'LoRa operates in the license free sub gigahertz radio frequency band' incl. 868 MHz (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following is true about the SIGFOX network in terms of messages and payload?
options: Up to 50 messages per day with a payload of 8 bytes per message
Up to 75 messages per day with a payload of 10 bytes per message
Up to 140 messages per day with a payload of 12 bytes per message
Up to 200 messages per day with a payload of 15 bytes per message
questions.explanation: 'up to 140 messages per day, with a payload of 12 bytes per message' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which library (header file) is used for interfacing the DHT22 sensor as demonstrated in the Hands On Industrial Environment Monitoring project?
questions.explanation: Demo uses the Adafruit DHT library for DHT22 (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)); that library's header is DHT.h (DHT22.h/DHT11.h/Adafruit_DHT.h are not its header).

questions.q: Which of the following topologies are supported by Zigbee?
questions.explanation: 'different topologies that are supported by ZigBee, star topology, tree topology, and mesh topology' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)); the 'Bus' answer in the 2025 copy is wrong.

questions.q: The physical and MAC layers of the Zigbee communication protocol is based on _______. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Zigbee follows IEEE 802.15.4 (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: “Xbee is a mesh communication protocol based on the IEEE 802.15.4 whereas Zigbee is the product that uses the Xbee communication protocol for radio communication.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: Reversed: 'ZigBee protocol is a mesh communication protocol based on IEEE 802.15.4 ... Xbee is a product from the company Digi' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following functions is performed by the coordinator node in a Zigbee network?
options: Acts as the root of the network and bridge between different networks
questions.explanation: Coordinator 'is the root of the network and it acts as the bridge between these different networks' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the data characteristics of IIoT processing?
options: Correlation in space, time, and other dimensions
questions.explanation: Polymorphism, temporal/causal relationships and correlation in space/time are all listed data characteristics (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is false about the rule-based engine?
options: Extract causal and temporal patterns using predefined rules
Handles multiple data streams and correlates them to provide meaningful output
Cannot process data in near real-time
Performs decision-making processes based on predefined rules
questions.explanation: Lecture stresses CEP must 'process the data in real near real-time' (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1), so 'cannot process data in near real-time' is the false one.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the limitation of current CEP systems?
options: Run-time update of threshold not possible
questions.explanation: Limitations of traditional CEP: 'manual thresholding ... specified beforehand manually' and 'not context aware'; micro-CEP adaptively updates thresholds (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following options is false about the services rendered by the Smart Water Management System?
questions.explanation: SWAMP offers 'replicable services ..., customizable service ..., application specific services' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2); non-replicable is false.

questions.q: “iRobot-Factory is a cognitive manufacturing factory which applies cognitive intelligence and edge computing for improved manufacturing.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: iRobot-Factory is about 'cognitive manufacturing' with components incl. 'edge computing node' and cloud cognitive engine (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following is false about the design of the SmartSantander?
questions.explanation: SmartSantander design considerations: 'experimentation realism, heterogeneity, scale, mobility, reliability, user involvement' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following represents a type of Industrial Control System?
questions.explanation: ICS types: PLC, DCS and SCADA (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following does not characterize big data analytics?
questions.explanation: Big data attributes: volume, velocity, variability, veracity, variety (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following algorithms is useful when it is feasible to acquire training data for the different states (or classes) that need to be modeled?
questions.explanation: 'supervised learning basically uses training data' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following is false about the deep learning models?
options: Learns features automatically without manually specifying them
Raw data from sensors can be directly fed into the model
Generally require a large amount of computation power
questions.explanation: 'most of these deep learning methods are based on traditional neural networks' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following software may be used for batch-oriented analytics?
questions.explanation: 'software such as Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark etc. may be used' for batch/distributed analytics (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a classification algorithm?
options: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise
questions.explanation: 'for classification SVM or Support Vector Machines' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: In ________ data points may belong to more than one cluster. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: 'Soft clustering ... certain points may belong to two or more clusters' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following supervised learning algorithms may be used when the output variable is a real number instead of a categorical value?
questions.explanation: 'regression is when the output variable is a real number' (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the reinforcement learning algorithm is false?
options: There is no external supervisor to guide the agent
Builds a knowledge graph from the constant feedback of the corresponding actions
There is a mapping between input and output
questions.explanation: RL has 'a reward-penalty structure'; it has no external supervisor, builds a knowledge graph from feedback, and has an input-output mapping (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: “Machine learning is a subset of deep learning that can learn automatically by finding the features of the object on its own.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: 'deep learning is a subset of machine learning. And machine learning itself is a subset of artificial intelligence' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Why is cloud computing necessary for IIoT?
options: High computational speed for data monitoring and analytics
questions.explanation: Need for cloud: high computational speed, storage, scalable/secure services, and data acquisition 'can be made much more efficient' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is not true about Platform-as-a-service for IIoT?
options: Clients have control over the application and the configuration environment
Software firms like Cumulocity, Bosch IoT, and Carriots offer PaaS for IoT industries
questions.explanation: PaaS: 'the clients over here have control over the applications and the configuration environment' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Who among the following does not provide Industrial Cloud Platform?
questions.explanation: Industrial cloud providers named: ThingWorx, Cumulocity, Uptake, C3 IoT, Meshify, GE Predix, etc. (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1); Netbeans is an IDE.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of using a Cloud simulator before real deployment?
questions.explanation: Not in the original lectures; a cloud simulator gives cost-free, repeatable pre-deployment testing, so all options apply.

questions.q: Which of the following does not represent the objective of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Industry 4.0 objectives: robust solutions, higher production, improved customer satisfaction, expanded security, improved performance (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: “K-medoid is a clustering algorithm that is used to maximize the distance between some randomly selected points in a cluster.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: Not in the original lectures; K-medoids minimizes the dissimilarity between points and the cluster medoid, it does not maximize distances.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a valid reason for employing fog computing in IIoT?

Need for immediate action and quick response
Data may be critical as well as time-sensitive

questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about the fog-enabled IIoT for Smart Grid and Power Industry?

Power supply is provided from micro-grids, local distribution companies
Advanced metering infrastructure for bi-directional communication
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): smart grid uses dynamic demand scheduling of appliances; smart grid/AMI communication is bidirectional, so 'unidirectional communication' is false.

questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): Nebbiolo 'have different products, Fog OS, FogNode, FogSM'. No fogBCD.

questions.q: SONM is a Decentralized Fog Computing Platform that renders distributed cloud services with fog as the backend. Which of the following facilities is not supported by SONM?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): SONM/'Swim' components support 'blockchain infrastructure, video streaming, machine learning, video rendering'; no digital triplet.

questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): variables are simply assigned (a = 20, x = 'hello', y = TRUE) with no type declaration.

questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'this cap is basically for power'.

questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): Julia data structures shown are tuples, dictionaries (Dict) and arrays.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the essential characteristics of cloud computing according to NIST?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop)/Lecture 39 (Cloud Computing in IIoT Part 1): cloud characteristics 'on demand self service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service'.

questions.q: Why is it necessary to perform integration which is a part of data pre-processing in the context of Data management?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'Integration talks about combination of data arriving from different sources and providing users with unified integrated view'.

questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'NoSQL databases ... key value database, column oriented database and document oriented database'.

questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'the master executes the operations like opening, closing, renaming files... Slaves ... read write request from the file system's clients' - roles reversed in statement, so False.

Provides multiple parallel short paths between any pair of server
Places intelligence on modular data center (MDC) servers
Forms multiple edge-disjoint server spanning tree

questions.q: Which of the following protocols is used by the SDN?
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): 'a very popular protocol which is known as the open flow protocol ... specifically designed' for SDN.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect about Software-defined networks (SDN)?
options: SDN increases the complexity of traditional networks by separating the control and data planes
SDN and NFV are separate paradigms
SDN provides a centralized view of the whole network which improves controllability, efficiency, and network stability
SDN can provide seamless transition of data routes, self-organization, configuration optimization, and smart transmissions
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): SDN decouples control and data planes to improve/simplify network management, not to increase complexity.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of the SDIIoT Architecture?
questions.explanation: Lecture 46 (SDN in IIoT Part 2): SDIIoT covers sensor networks, public networks, industrial cloud, industrial bus networks - not private network.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of the SDWSN platform in the context of Industry 4.0?
questions.explanation: Lecture 46 (SDN in IIoT Part 2): SD sensor network has data plane, control plane and applications.

questions.q: Data processing is generally performed in ________ present in the SDIIoT architecture?
questions.explanation: Lecture 46 (SDN in IIoT Part 2): industrial cloud control plane has 'process unit monitoring, data processing service ...'.

questions.q: R stands for _________ in STRIDE Threat Model of IoT security. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): STRIDE - 'Repudiation ... you send the data and later on you deny'.

questions.q: Application layer of the IoT attack surface is vulnerable to which of the following IIoT Attack Vectors?
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): reversal attack is an application-layer vector; MITM is network, jamming is physical.

questions.q: What does trust permeation aim to establish within the IIoT system?
questions.explanation: Lecture 47 (Security in IIoT Part 1): 'trust permeation ... hierarchical flow of trust ... IIoT system consists of many units; design, development, manufacturing logistics' - trust across unit hierarchies.

questions.q: Which of the following does not represent the building blocks of IIoT security framework?
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): building blocks - end device, fog device, cloud security, data protection, communication protection, security management.

questions.q: Which of the following standards is supported by the OT security of IIoT?

questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): OT standards like IEC 62443 and NIST ones; slide's OT list includes NERC-CIP, whereas ISO/IEC 15408 is IT and ISO 27017/NIST SP 800-144/ENISA are cloud standards.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a key component of cloud security of IIoT framework?
questions.explanation: Lecture 48 (Security in IIoT Part 2): cloud security - 'physical security, data privacy, security controls, identity management and access control'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a key feature of smart factory?
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): features connected, optimized, transparent, proactive, agile.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect about Kuka – an IoT-Enabled Factory?

Deployed on the A330 and A350 final assembly lines in Toulouse
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): A330/A350 Toulouse lines belong to Airbus factory of the future, not Kuka.

questions.q: _________ is carried out by Amazon – Robotic Shelves. Fill in the blanks.
options: AR app based end-to-end factory floor view
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): Amazon robotic shelves 'robots can efficiently locate and search different items'.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect about Maersk – Intelligent Shipping?
options: It is a container shipping company
Uses IoT for preserving refrigerated containers
Does not use blockchain technology for supply chain optimization
Tracks assets and fuel consumption using sensors
questions.explanation: Lecture 49 (Factories and Assembly Line): Maersk 'uses blockchain technology for supply chain optimization'.

questions.q: Which of the following represents the applications of IoT in Livestock Barns?
options: Soil moisture sensors optimize irrigation and fertilization
questions.explanation: Lecture 50 (Food Industry): 'in the live stock barns sensors can help in monitoring the health parameters of different animals'.

questions.q: In the context of Agricultural IoT, what do we mean by LAI?
questions.explanation: LAI = Leaf Area Index, a standard crop-monitoring parameter in agricultural IoT; other options are nonsense.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are a challenge faced by IoT in healthcare?
options: Devices use low-power battery hence have short battery life
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide 'IoT Healthcare Challenges': less computational capability, less on-device memory, energy limitation (low power battery).

questions.q: What is the general action of healthcare body sensors in case some abnormalities are detected?
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide: sensors collect BP, respiration, etc. 'It triggers alarm, if any abnormal situation is there'.

questions.q: Confidentiality, Integrity, __________ and Availability are the four security cornerstones of IIoT based Healthcare monitoring and management.
questions.explanation: L51 'IIoT Applications: Healthcare' slide 'IIoT Healthcare Security Requirement': Confidentiality, Integrity, Authentication, Availability.

questions.q: Optimization and Autonomy are the features of which among the following IIoT models in the Power sector?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants' slide 'IIoT Maturity Model': Monitor -> Control -> Optimization -> Autonomy.

questions.q: In Smart grids supported by IIoT, data communication network is not integrated with the physical power transmission network?
questions.explanation: L52 'IIoT Applications: Power Plants': smart grid carries both power flow and information flow (WAN/NAN/HAN) together; the networks are integrated, so the statement is False.

options: Statement 1 is correct but 2 is not
Statement 1 is incorrect while 2 is correct
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': passive tags have no internal power source; active tags have batteries and 'longer range and memory than the passive RFID tags'.

questions.q: IIoT can be deployed in inventory management to automate which of the following activities?
questions.explanation: L53 'Inventory Management & Quality Control': 'the stocking in and stocking out ... can be done efficiently with the incorporation of IIoT'.

questions.q: In the context of Network Security, what does behavioral analytics deal with?
options: Detects abnormal behavior by the network
Establishes a connection between the sender and receiver
Generates new routes across the network
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide 'Types of Network Security': 'Behavioral analytics - Detection of abnormal behavior by the network'.

questions.q: IP rights are a risk when using AR/VR?
questions.explanation: L54 'Plant Security and Safety' slide 'Risks (AR/VR)': lists 'Intellectual Property (IP) rights'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a stakeholder in Facility Management?
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management': stakeholders/dimensions are buildings, finance, people, contracts; patents are not listed.

questions.q: Which of the following challenges arise due to ageing of inventory?

Recurring taxation levied by the Government
questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' slide challenges: 'Ageing inventory - Need for proactive preventive and maintenance procedures'.

questions.q: In IIoT enabled facility management, logically where do subcontractors are located?

As a part of the customers
As a master authority of the owners

questions.explanation: L55 'Facility Management' slide 'Optimization': optimized usage of resources - manpower, assets, technology, cost-effectiveness.

questions.q: Real time and easy diagnosis are ________ of Healthcare IoT?

questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry': chemical-industry benefits include improve logistics (others are inverted).

questions.q: What is/are the benefits of using IoT sensors in the Pharmaceutical Industry?
options: Access huge data of different manufacturing departments
questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' pharma slide: access huge data, real time monitoring, reduce production cost and wastage.

questions.explanation: L56 'Oil, Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry' slide: detect ADR, effects of pharmaceutical excipients, allergies.

questions.q: UAVs are capable of performing which of the following operations?
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' slide: 'UAVs are capable of taking aerial imagery, visual imagery, thermal imagery and also radio-frequency imagery'.

Improved safety and regulatory, platform and payload adaptability, automated safety modes, intelligent piloting models and full autonomy, airspace awareness
questions.explanation: L57 'UAVs in Industries' generations slide: First - 'Fundamental Remote Control UAVs of different forms'.

Require more time, energy and money

Covers local areas with high cost

Measure the carbon storage in biomass by remote sensing

questions.explanation: L58 'Case Studies for Industry 4.0 & IIoT' slide: case study enables a researcher to closely examine data within a specific context, follows certain procedures, provides quantitative and qualitative analysis.

Optimize use of seed, fertilizer, water

The difference between standard and measured values

Packet transmission in Low-power and lossy networks (LLN)

Use of artificial intelligence and machine learning

All the actions required for a product from order to delivery

Systems that operate only on computational components
Interacting networks of physical and computational components

A social media platform for employees

Storing multiple copies of each data element
Using outdated software for decision making
Storing the same data across different systems

A wide field of view with head-mounted displays and motion detecting devices
Only visual feedback without interaction with the user
Manual control over the real environment

A program with AI uses a large database and algorithmic search method
A program with AI uses a large knowledge base and heuristic search method
A program without AI uses a large database and heuristic search method

Lock’s the user’s computer files by using an encryption and demands some money to unlock them

questions.explanation: L19: 'sensors are basically the primary source of IIoT data'.

questions.q: Which component is NOT part of the configurations involved in smart sensors?
questions.explanation: L19: smart sensor configurations are 'multi parameter sensing unit ... analog detection circuit, digital signal conditioning unit, and interfacing unit to the bus'.

questions.q: What is the role of conventional sensing in industrial control systems?
options: To increase the complexity of systems
To involve feedback automation of a process
To disconnect systems from feedback loops
To reduce the reliability of systems
questions.explanation: L19: 'conventional sensing it involved getting some kind of feedback, automation of a process, in an industrial control system'.

questions.q: Which sector is predicted to have the highest growth in Industry 4.0 as per PwC’s Global Industry 4.0 Survey of 2016?
questions.explanation: L20 shows the sector growth chart (electronics, manufacturing, defense, transportation, chemical, automotive, construction) and highlights electronics: 'current growth trend is about 40 to 50 percent ... predicted ... 70 to 80, so it is a huge leap'. The chart values for other sectors are not read out.

questions.q: What is the focus of the ‘Control Layer’ in the 5C Architecture for Cyber Physical Systems?
questions.explanation: L20: 'the control layer ... supervised control, then ... self-configuration, self-optimization, self-adjustment'.

questions.q: In the existing GSM cellular phones, a smart card is used to provide security to e-commerce applications, using encryption and digital signatures. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Not in the transcripts; the smart card in GSM/WAP phones that gives e-commerce security through encryption and digital signatures is the Wireless Identity Module (WIM). TPM is a PC chip.

questions.q: Which of the following is an inclusion in the Industry 4.0 application as per ICP DAS?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): ICP DAS M2M sector covers 'supply chain automation, logistics, motion control'.

questions.q: Which technology does Caterpillar integrate with IoT for enhanced machine interaction?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Caterpillar uses IoT and augmented reality.

questions.q: What is the objective of the Cisco & Fanuc smart factory initiative?
questions.explanation: Lecture 21 (Industrial Processes - Part 2): Cisco & Fanuc smart factory 'objective is to minimize the downtime in the industrial facility'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the building blocks of a business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): building blocks listed; employee satisfaction is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of customer segment?
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): segments: mass, niche, segmented, diversified, multi-sided.

questions.q: What is a characteristic of the Subscription Model in IoT business models?
options: Recurring revenue through regular subscription fees
questions.explanation: Lecture 22 (Business Models - Part 1): subscription model - not a one-time charge; fees charged on periodic usage, recurring revenue.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of IIoT business model?
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IIoT models are cloud-based, service-oriented, process-oriented.

questions.q: What is an SLA in the context of business transactions?
questions.explanation: SLA = service-level agreement (standard term; not a lecture topic).

questions.q: What does Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) provide?
options: Only software online in the cloud
Required hardware and software online in the cloud
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): IaaS - hardware/computing infrastructure offered as a service (slide: required hardware and software online).

questions.q: Which business model aims at process optimization within a company and across company
questions.explanation: Lecture 23 (Business Models - Part 2): process-oriented model - 'processes will have to be optimized within a company, and across different company borders'.

questions.q: What type of KPI is input-oriented and hard to measure?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): leading KPI 'is input-oriented, and is hard to measure'.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major focus and activity of Industrial Internet Consortium (IIC) members?
questions.explanation: Lecture 24 (Reference Architecture - Part 1): 'testbeds are an area of major focus and activity of the different IIC members'.

questions.q: What does the Usage Viewpoint in IIRA relate to?
options: Key capabilities identified in the business viewpoint and activities coordinating different units of work
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'usage viewpoints are related with the key capabilities that are identified in the business viewpoint and the activities that coordinate the different units of work'.

questions.q: What are the elements of an activity in the Usage Viewpoint of IIRA?
options: Vision, Values, Key Objectives, Fundamental Capabilities
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): activity elements are trigger, workflow, effects and constraints.

questions.q: Which viewpoint relates to the technical representation of an IIoT system, including interfaces and protocols?
questions.explanation: Lecture 25 (Reference Architecture - Part 2): 'Implementation viewpoint relates to the technical presentation of the IIoT system ... interconnection of different components'.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the benefits of sensor usage in industry?
options: Increasing downtime due to routine maintenance
Reduced manual intervention for sensing in hazardous areas
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): sensors improve safety, monitoring, remote diagnostics; the other options are not benefits.

questions.q: Ultrasonic sensors can be used for – Fill in the blank.
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1): ultrasonic sensors 'used for object detection, measuring distance, dynamic body detection'.

questions.q: Which sensor can be used for distance measurement, pattern matching, color checking, structured lighting, and motion capture?
questions.explanation: Lecture 26 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 1) lists image sensors without detail; distance measurement, pattern matching, color checking, structured lighting, motion capture are image-sensor uses (PIR/ultrasonic uses are given separately).

questions.q: What is another name for MOS gas sensors?
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'MOS gas sensors are chemi-resistive gas sensors'.

questions.q: What is the ‘Optimum Temperature’ in the context of MOS gas sensors?
options: The temperature at which the sensor does not respond
The temperature at which the sensor gives the best response
The lowest temperature at which the sensor operates
The highest temperature the sensor can withstand
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): 'a particular temperature at which the sensor gives the best response ... that is optimum temperature'.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a gas sensor when it detects Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)?
options: The resistance changes from its baseline resistance
questions.explanation: Lecture 27 (Key Enablers: Sensing - Part 2): on sensing VOCs 'their resistive properties change with respect to the baseline resistance'.

questions.q: What are the typical requirements for industrial communication?
options: High duty-cycle, high latency, high jitter
Real-time, very low duty-cycle, very low latency, very low jitter
Manual data processing, high latency, low duty-cycle
High duty-cycle, low latency, high jitter
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): real-time, 'very low duty cycle', 'very low latency', 'very low jitter'.

questions.q: What is the range of data transmission rate for EtherCat?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'range of data transmission in EtherCAT is typically ... about 200 Mbps'.

questions.q: Which topology is the EtherNet/IP standard based on?
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): 'Ethernet IP uses the star topology'.

questions.q: Which Profibus variant handles communication between PCs and Programmable Logic Controllers?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): 'Profibus FMS ... handles the communication between the PCs and the PLCs'.

questions.q: Which Profibus variant is suitable for hazardous environments?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Profibus PA/MBP for hazardous environments.

questions.q: Which network topology does the Interbus use?
questions.explanation: Lecture 29 (Connectivity - Part 2): Interbus ring topology.

questions.q: What is the latency supported by Tactile Internet?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): 'low end-to-end latency of less than 1 millisecond RTT'.

questions.q: Which frequency band does the 5G NR use for high-band communication?
questions.explanation: Lecture 30 (Connectivity - Part 3): high band > 24 GHz.

questions.q: What are the three components of the Modbus architecture?
options: Modbus Node, Modbus Junction, Modbus Branch
Modbus Client, Modbus Router, Modbus Server
Modbus Publisher, Modbus Broker, Modbus Subscribers.
Modbus Master, Modbus Gateway, Modbus Slaves
questions.explanation: Lecture 28 (Connectivity - Part 1): Modbus TCP firmware example - PLC/HMI/SCADA masters over Ethernet to a device master (gateway) and Modbus serial slaves.

questions.q: _______________stands for L in LPWAN. Fill in the blanks
questions.explanation: LPWAN = low power wide area network (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: In which of the following radio bands does the SIGFOX radio link operate?
questions.explanation: 'unlicensed ISM radio bands' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: The wireless throughput achieved by SIGFOX is up to ……………..bits per second. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: 'throughput ... using SIGFOX is up to 100 bps' (Lecture 31: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 4 (LoRa/SIGFOX + NodeMCU demo)).

questions.q: Which IEEE standard is the physical and MAC layer of Zigbee based on?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.15.4 (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: “Zigbee’s communication ranges typically vary between 10-100 meters depending on the device variant.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: 'The communication range in ZigBee varies from 10 to 100 meters' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: Which of the following is a product by Digi?
questions.explanation: 'Xbee is a product from the company Digi' (Lecture 32: Key Enablers of IIoT: Connectivity – Part 5 (Zigbee/Xbee demo)).

questions.q: What is the full form of CPS that seamlessly monitors and controls the physical processes by integrating computational and physical components?
questions.explanation: CPS = Cyber Physical Systems (used throughout the processing/analytics lectures); other expansions are not real terms.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are true about rule-based engines in the context of Complex Event Processing?
options: Extract causal and temporal patterns using predefined rules
Handles multiple data streams and correlates them to provide meaningful output
Can process data in near real-time
questions.explanation: Extract causal/temporal patterns, correlate event streams from different sources, process in near real-time — all attributed to rule-based CEP (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is false about middleware in the context of IIoT processing?
options: It is the software layer between the infrastructure layer and the application layer
It provides services according to device functionality
It does not support for heterogeneity, security
Many middleware solutions are based on service-oriented architecture
questions.explanation: Middleware provides services per device functionality, handles heterogeneity and security, many are SOA-based (Lecture 33: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 1); (c) is the false one.

questions.q: The SWAMP project developed IoT-based methods and approaches for smart water management in the precision irrigation domain. Which of the following services can be rendered by Smart Water Management Platform?
questions.explanation: SWAMP services: replicable services, customizable services for water management/distribution, application-specific services (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: “The objectives of Vineyard Health Monitoring is to increase the yield and quality of grapes with optimal water use.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: Vineyard monitoring objective: 'increase yield, quality of grapes and optimal use of water' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: SmartSantander is an IoT-based smart city deployment platform for large-scale applications. What does AAA stand for in its architecture layer?
questions.explanation: 'authentication authorization accounting' (Lecture 34: Key Enablers of IIoT: Processing – Part 2).

questions.q: “Open Loop Control is never used to control decisions independent of process variables in Industrial Control Systems.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: 'open loop ... the control decision is made independent of the process variable' (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control) — so 'never used' is false.

questions.q: _____________is a type of Industrial Control Systems. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: SCADA is one of the three ICS types (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a component of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition?
questions.explanation: SCADA components include telemetry units, SCADA master units, HMI (Lecture 35: Key Enablers of IIoT: Process Control); 'Remote Telephonic Units' is not one.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about unsupervised methods?
options: They require labeled data to function.
They find structure in the input data on their own.
They are always more accurate than supervised methods.
They are not at all useful for clustering tasks.
questions.explanation: 'unsupervised learning methods basically extract a structure ... in the input data on their own' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: “Deployment of IIoT analytics typically consists of three steps – i) train a (predictive) analytics model, ii) test and validate the model on previously unseen data, and iii) deploy the model to make predictions on real (streaming) data.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: 'train a model ... test and validate ... on some previously unseen data and thereafter deploy that model to make predictions on ... data ... streamed in real time' (Lecture 36: IIoT Analytics and Data Management: Introduction).

questions.q: ……………………….requires fine-tuning a trained model. This approach requires less amount of data. Therefore, the time required for processing and computation may be reduced from hours to minutes and from weeks to days. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Not in the original lectures; fine-tuning a pretrained model with less data is transfer learning.

questions.q: Which of the following is false about Reinforcement Learning?
options: There is an external supervisor to guide the agent.
There is a reward function which acts as feedback to the agent.
It builds a knowledge graph from the constant feedback of the corresponding actions.
questions.explanation: RL has 'a reward-penalty structure'; it has no external supervisor, builds a knowledge graph from feedback, and has an input-output mapping (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following machine learning techniques is used to identify similar groups of data, coined as clustering?
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning identifies similar groups — clustering (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: In………… one data point may belong to more than one cluster. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: FCM (Lecture 37: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 1).

questions.q: “Machine learning is a subset of deep learning which can learn automatically by finding the features of the object on its own.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: Reversed: DL is a subfield of ML that learns features on its own (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: When does a deep learning model typically provide better accuracy?
options: When the amount of data is very limited
When the amount of data is huge
questions.explanation: 'DL gives improved performance with respect to accuracy when the data volume increases' (Lecture 38: Machine Learning and Data Science – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following can be achieved by deploying cloud in IIoT?
options: High computational speed for data monitoring and analytics
Storage of huge amounts of data
questions.explanation: High computational speed, storage, scalable/secure services (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following services can NOT be provided by utilizing cloud computing?
questions.explanation: SaaS, PaaS, IaaS (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is rendered by a Consumer IoT cloud platform?
options: A large number of data points
questions.explanation: Consumer IoT clouds have 'modest levels of security'; large data points, QoS and ROI belong to industrial IoT clouds (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: MindSphere is the cloud-based, open IoT operating system. Which of the following features are supported by the MindSphere?
options: Automated exploitation of performance and intelligence
questions.explanation: MindSphere features: 'security support ... procurement and distribution ... automated exploration of performance and intelligence' (Lecture 39: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 1).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a C3 IoT Platform tool?
questions.explanation: C3 IoT tools: Data Integrator, IDE, Data Explorer, Analytics Designer, Ex Machina, Data Science Notebook, Type Designer (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2) — not 'Type Developer'.

questions.q: “Cashify is an Industrial IoT platform that facilitates real-time monitoring and low-cost solutions.” State true or false.
questions.explanation: That description is of Meshify, not Cashify (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about fog computing?
options: An added layer between the edge and the cloud layer
Distributed at one level, centralized on the other
Intelligent in providing services like filtering, aggregation, and translation
questions.explanation: 'fog cannot do everything ... it is not that fog layer can do all the processing' (Lecture 40: Cloud Computing in IIoT – Part 2); 'fog does not stand on its own' (Lecture 41: Fog Computing in IIoT).

questions.q: Why is fog computing important for IIoT applications?
options: To decrease the cloud storage capacity
To provision immediate action and quick response to time-sensitive data
To eliminate the need for provisioning data security
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): time-sensitive critical data needs 'immediate action or quicker response'.

questions.q: Which of the following IIoT solutions can be rendered using Fog?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): 'fog advanced hardware and software features such as virtualization, automation, communication, analysis, prediction'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a fog platform provider?
questions.explanation: Lecture 41 (Fog Computing in IIoT): providers FogHorn, Nebbiolo, Crosser, Sonm; DHT11 is a temperature/humidity sensor.

questions.q: “Reserve words in R programming language have special meanings and can be used as variable names and function names.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): reserved words 'have some special meaning and ... cannot be used as a variable name'.

questions.q: Which of the following methods is the correct format for declaring a variable in the R programming language?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'a equal to 20' assignment (A=10) is valid; A->10 and #A=>10 are invalid (duplicate option text is a scraping artifact).

questions.q: ………..syntax is used by Julia programming language to print in the console. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'println ... is used for printing'.

questions.q: ……….is the data type available in the R programming language. Fill in the blanks.
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): data types logical, numeric, integer, complex, character, raw; TRUE/else/break are reserved words.

questions.q: Which of the following syntax is used to load the package in R programming language?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): 'library caret ... will basically help you in loading these libraries'.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about the Julia programming language?
questions.explanation: Lecture 42 (Tutorial for R & Julia): Julia is open source, supports distributed computation/parallelism and C function calls; Julia has full Unicode support, so 'does not support Unicode' is false.

questions.q: Which of the following file systems is derived from the open-source codes of Google File System?
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): HDFS listed with GFS; Hadoop is 'open source implementation for GFS and MapReduce'.

questions.q: “Hadoop is an open-source implementation for Google File System and MapReduce.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: Lecture 43 (Data Management with Hadoop): 'open source implementation for GFS and MapReduce'.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a property of Data Center Networks?
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks): desirable properties stable, secure, reliable, scalable, agile - not rigid.

questions.q: Which of the following represent(s) data center network topologies?
questions.explanation: Lecture 44 (Data Center Networks): four topologies three-tier, fat-tree, DCell, BCube.

questions.q: “In Software Defined Networking (SDN), forwarding devices forward an incoming traffic based on the control logic defined by the SDN controller.” State True or False.
questions.explanation: Lecture 45 (SDN in IIoT Part 1): 'forwarding devices that forward the incoming traffic based on certain control logic ... defined by the SDN controller'.

questions.q: A ______ consists of single or multiple public, community, or private fog nodes, which are logically combined to provide services to multiple organizations. Fill in the blank.
questions.explanation: NIST fog deployment models (private/community/public/hybrid fog node): a hybrid fog node is a composition of two or more private, community or public fog nodes.
